newsitem.title: japan: TIFFE Euroyen end slightly higher ahead "tankan".
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen end slightly higher ahead "tankan".

text.p: Key June three-month Euroyen futures ended slightly higher on Tuesday due to a sharp rise in Japanese government bonds (JGBs).
"JGBs were not sold, despite earlier fears that the auction results would not be that good," a trader at a city bank said.
The rise in JGBs helped support Euroyen futures, the trader said.
Turnover of the June contract was 28,726 contracts.

Traders said Euroyen futures were unlikely to be affected much by the Bank of Japan's key "tankan" corporate sentiment survey due out on Wednesday if the results were within market expectations, traders said.
They said the average market forecast of the November diffusion index (DI) for big manufacturers, an important gauge of corporate sentiment, was around minus two or minus three.
If, however, the tankan's forecast of the DI for March were to come in at around plus four or plus five, this could cause some fluctuation in the market, a trader at another city bank said.
The average market prediction for the tankan's forecast of the key DI for March was around zero or plus one, the first trader said.
The tankan data is scheduled to be released at 8.50 a.m. on Wednesday (2350 GMT Tuesday).
Traders said the market did not believe the release of the tankan would lead to an immediate change in the BOJ's monetary policy.
The key overnight call rate had fallen to 0.48 percent as of 0734 GMT, down from the previous day's weighted average of 0.49 percent.
Traders said Tuesday's weighted average was likely to be 0.48 percent.
The BOJ injected 400 billion yen into the money market in the morning, maintaining its neutral money market stance.
Key three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) were not issued on Tuesday, and were tagged with a sell quote of 0.51 percent.
Two- and one-month CDs were also tagged with sell quotes, of 0.50 percent and 0.49 percent, respectively.
The CD rates were unchanged from the previous day.
